text.p: Bonds gained with the shorter end of the curve up to four years well-supported by confidence another rate cut in Portugal would not be long delayed.
Few traders or analysts expect the Bank of Portugal to cut again today when it announces money market conditions after it knocked 30 basis points off the repo last Friday.

But some traders said that the gains in the longer end, with the spread with the Bunds narrowing to 66 basis points and widening to 14 basis points with Spain's Bonos, was taking the market into dangerous territory where it could be vulnerable to profit-taking.
"They are dangerous levels," said one trader.

Traders said that the longer end was being supported by a relative lack of supply and that that this factor was stretching the spread beyond what would be a logical gap of a negative five to 10 basis points with Spain.
"The escudo is slightly steadier, the Bank of Portugal may not cut (rates) today, but it has room," said one trader.
But he added that it was necessary not to forget the Federal Reserve meeting set for May 20, which could see a U.S. rate rise, and the French elections.
